jobs.title: Workforce Management Planning Analyst
jobs.jd_full:
Thumbtack helps millions of people confidently care for their homes.

Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. Every day in every county of the U.S., people turn to Thumbtack to complete urgent repairs, seasonal maintenance and bigger improvements. We help homeowners know which projects to do, when to do them and who to hire from our growing community of 300,000 local service businesses. If making an impact inspires you, join us. Imagine what we’ll build together.

About the Workforce Management Team

Our Workforce Management (WFM) team ensures operational stability by combining smart planning with real-time execution. We forecast demand, develop staffing plans, build schedules, and make adjustments in real time to keep performance on track and minimize disruptions. By protecting service commitments and driving consistency, we help Thumbtack deliver a seamless, reliable experience that builds long-term trust with pros and customers.

About the role

As a Workforce Analyst, you’ll work across the full workforce management cycle — forecasting demand, building schedules, and managing intraday performance — so that customers and pros get reliable, timely support. This hybrid role connects long-range planning with day-to-day execution, giving you a complete view of how staffing decisions shape service outcomes.

You’ll own work of moderate scope with a blend of autonomy and manager support, apply team standards and decision frameworks, and grow your domain expertise by tackling increasingly complex challenges. It’s an ideal next step for a practitioner who wants to build depth across planning, scheduling, and real-time management.

What you’ll do

Forecasting & Capacity

  • Forecast call, case, and task volumes across channels, adjusting for seasonality, campaigns, and business events.

  • Translate forecasts into staffing requirements and capacity plans that balance service performance, utilization, and cost.

  • Compare forecasts against actuals, explain variance, and refine assumptions to improve accuracy over time.

Scheduling & Allocation

  • Build and maintain schedules, shifts, and rotations that meet coverage needs within business constraints.

  • Plan around training, PTO, and project time while keeping scheduling fair and transparent for agents.

  • Allocate staff across queues and skills to meet service goals efficiently.

Intraday Management

  • Monitor real-time queues, adherence, and service levels across channels.

  • Take tactical action when conditions change, such as re-queuing, shift adjustments, or overtime, weighing service, cost, and agent impact.

  • Communicate status, interventions, and escalations clearly and quickly to operations partners.

Analytics & Recommendations

  • Track utilization, shrinkage, adherence, and forecast accuracy to surface trends and improvement opportunities.

  • Deliver clear reporting and insights that inform headcount planning, budgeting, and operational decisions.

  • Diagnose root causes of performance gaps and propose practical, system-aware improvements.

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Partner with Operations, HR, Training, and Finance to keep planning assumptions and cadences aligned.

  • Document assumptions, flag changes early, and maintain reliable planning records others depend on.

  • Contribute to WFM processes and team initiatives that improve how we work.

In order to be successful, you must bring

  • 3+ years of experience in workforce management, with hands-on work in at least two of forecasting, scheduling, and real-time analysis.

  • Solid understanding of demand and staffing drivers, and the judgment to combine data with business context to build realistic forecasts and plans.

  • Calm, sound decision-making when service conditions change quickly, following consistent frameworks while adapting when needed.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, using data from multiple sources to find root causes and weigh risks and benefits.

  • Ability to turn data into clear, simple insights and explain the “why” behind recommendations to different audiences.

  • Proficiency with workforce management systems, reporting tools, and spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets).

  • Organized, transparent working habits: documenting assumptions, sharing context early, and following through on commitments.

  • A collaborative, proactive mindset, seeking out best practices and opportunities to improve how the team operates.

jobs.title: Director of Procurement & Raw Materials Strategy
jobs.jd_full:
About Bobbie

Bobbie makes European-style organic infant formula manufactured end-to-end in the U.S., because we believe every parent deserves to feed their baby with confidence, without judgment and without compromise. No mystery ingredients. No shortcuts. Just clean, thoughtfully made formula that parents can trust.

But Bobbie has never been just a formula company. When the 2022 national infant formula shortage left parents across the country unable to feed their babies, we closed our storefront to new customers rather than leave a single existing family without formula. We went to Washington. We got loud. And we opened our Heath, Ohio manufacturing facility to make sure something like that could never happen again.

That's who we are, and that's what you'd be joining.

Bobbie for Change

Our advocacy arm, Bobbie for Change, exists because making great formula isn't enough if the systems around parenthood are still broken. We fight for paid federal parental leave, push for legislation to prevent future formula shortages, advocate for feeding equity, and support families navigating impossible situations, including donating formula to parents impacted by breast and gynecologic cancers through the Bobbie Breasties program.

We're a company that genuinely believes becoming a parent makes you an activist. The people who work here feel that too.

About the Role

Bobbie is a $150M+ infant nutrition company growing 50% year over year, expanding into new product categories while operating under FDA-regulated infant formula standards. The Director, Procurement & Raw Materials Strategy is a newly created role that will own strategic sourcing and supplier management for the ingredients and packaging behind that growth, reporting directly to the VP, Supply Chain.

One person currently handles procurement strategy, supplier negotiation, tactical buying, and cost tracking. This director will take ownership of the strategic side of that work, build the cost accounting and supplier performance infrastructure, and free the current purchasing team to focus on category execution and supplier relationships.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Sourcing & Supplier Management

  • Own supplier strategy across dairy and nutritional ingredients, other ingredients and premixes, and packaging: a base of roughly 25 approved suppliers today, growing as Bobbie enters new categories.
  • Lead negotiation of multi-year supply agreements and master supply agreements.
  • Qualify and onboard new suppliers as Bobbie launches into new product categories, weighing lead time, cost, and regulatory risk, including FDA and IFN clearance timing on new packaging and ingredients.
  • Build a formal supplier qualification process and scorecards where none exist today.

Cost Accounting & Systems

  • Stand up cost accounting and PPV reporting for raw material and packaging spend, replacing the manual spreadsheet tracking the team relies on today.
  • Own procurement's use of ERP for planning, MRP, PO issuance, and item costing, partnering with the supply chain systems function to improve it over time.
  • Work with Finance to manage the PO approval thresholds tied to cash-timing, balancing raw material lead times against cash management needs.

Team Leadership

  • Manage and develop the purchasing team.
  • Shift the team's day-to-day from reactive tactical buying toward proactive category strategy and supplier relationship management.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with Quality, Regulatory, and Science on ingredient and packaging specifications, supplier audits, and regulatory clearance timing.
  • Partner with Supply Planning and Plant Operations, including comanufacturing sites, on demand signals, lead times, and inventory positioning.
  • Partner with Finance on cash-timing, PO approval workflows, and cost reporting.
  • Support new product launches end to end from a procurement standpoint: supplier selection, PO timing against regulatory clearance, and managing the tradeoffs of ordering ahead of clearance when launch timelines require it.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years in procurement or strategic sourcing, including experience negotiating multi-year supply agreements, ideally in food, CPG, or another regulated manufacturing environment.
  • Experience standing up or significantly improving cost accounting or PPV processes.
  • Comfort working directly in an ERP system and building reporting where none exists today.
  • Experience managing suppliers through new product launches, including regulatory-driven timelines.
  • People leadership experience, with comfort both setting strategy and staying close enough to the details to unblock the team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Dairy or nutritional ingredient sourcing experience.
  • Experience in infant formula, baby food, or another FDA-regulated food category.
  • Experience scaling a procurement function inside a high-growth company (50%+ year over year growth).

You’re inspired by our core values:

  • Be Radical - We are change makers, rule breakers and stigma shakers. We are unapologetically bold and use our megaphone for good.
  • Nurture the Tension - Parenthood is full of healthy tension, and so is building a company. We embrace the unknowns, practice humility and are a culture of learners.
  • Deliver Ounce by Ounce - Our customers have entrusted us to feed their babies. We lose sleep over the details, so they don’t have to.
  • Don’t Assume - We embrace our unique perspectives, withhold judgment, and find beauty in the paths that brought us all to Bobbie. Our strength is celebrating each other and our collective voice.

Compensation and Benefits:

Compensation

Our salaries are based on paying competitively for our size and industry. For fully remote roles, we have a salary range per role that is differentiated based on geographic location (Group A, B, or C).

  • Group A (SF/Bay Area, Seattle, NYC): $170,100–$200,000
  • Group B (Los Angeles, Chicago, Austin, Denver, Boston, Washington DC, San Diego, Philadelphia, Portland, Sacramento): $153,100 - $180,000
  • Group C (All Other Cities): $144,600 - $170,000

Benefits

  • Competitive stock options
  • 401k with employer match
  • Employee medical, dental, and vision insurance 100% covered by Bobbie, with options to add dependents through a subsidized pre-tax deduction
  • US-based remote work model
  • Flexible Time Off Policy (including Summer Fridays; half days on Fridays Memorial Day through Labor Day)
  • 16 paid company holidays, plus an end of year holiday shut down
  • 16 weeks of paid parental leave with the option to take an additional 8 months unpaid
  • One year subscription to Bobbie
  • $75 monthly internet stipend
  • Co-working space reimbursement

At Bobbie, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive company. We seek to create a culture where everyone can belong because we believe that people do their best work when they can show up every day as their authentic selves. We welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and perspectives.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Our Mission and Opportunity

Early education is one of the most important determinants of childhood outcomes, a critical support for working families, and a $175B market that remains underserved by modern technology. Brightwheel is the largest, fastest growing, and most loved platform in early ed, trusted by millions of educators and families every day. We are a three-time Cloud 100 company, backed by top investors including Addition, Bessemer, Emerson Collective, Lowercase Capital, Notable Capital, and Mark Cuban.

Our Team

Our team is passionate, talented, and customer-focused. We embody our Leadership Principles in our work and culture. We are a distributed team with remote employees across every US time zone, as well as select offices in the US and internationally.

Who You Are

You're an AI-native product leader and builder who thrives in high-ownership environments. You're energized by the full spectrum of the job — from iterating on live features to investing in greenfield 0→1 bets — and you have the judgment to know when to pursue each. You're comfortable in ambiguity, decisive under pressure, and relentless about customer and business impact.

You will succeed in this role if you are:

  • Focused on customer and business impact. You care about creating real value for educators and families, and about proving a business that's worth growing

  • A practitioner-builder. You don't lead from a distance. You use AI and modern tooling in your own work to build, prototype, and learn, and to show what great looks like

  • Motivated by ownership. You want a large surface area and the full portfolio that comes with it — from finding product-market fit and proving out a business model on a 0→1 bet, to removing pain points on existing, heavily used features

  • A generalist by instinct. You're drawn to whichever problem matters most right now, and you don't need the problem space to be familiar to make progress in it

What You’ll Do

Brightwheel sits at the center of early education, trusted by tens of thousands of schools and millions of families. We have more high-value opportunities than we have product managers, and you'll own one of them end to end.

The most likely starting point is enrollment — how schools fill their open seats and keep the families they already have. A center licensed for 50 children running at 42 is leaving real money on the table every month, and today the work of chasing inquiries, running tours, and confirming re-enrollment happens across inboxes and spreadsheets. Some of what schools need already exists in brightwheel. Some of it doesn't. You'll build both, and build the business around it.

This is an individual contributor role with significant scope — one of the broadest product mandates at brightwheel, with direct partnership with our CEO and executive team from day one.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the vision, strategy, and execution for a high-impact product area — from growing what already works to defining and launching what doesn't exist yet

  • Make the case for where we invest next, with evidence — including what to stop

  • Set appetite, scope accordingly, and hold your team to a high bar on speed, quality, and customer impact

  • Shape pricing and go-to-market for new capabilities you launch — from packaging to validating willingness to pay

  • Drive AI into the product in ways that genuinely improve outcomes for providers, staff, and families — not as a checkbox

  • Define success metrics, track performance, and communicate progress and tradeoffs clearly to leadership

  • Partner tightly with engineering and design to ship with urgency, unblock the team, and keep them focused on what matters

  • Contribute to brightwheel's product culture — raise the bar for product quality, velocity, and customer impact

What You've Done

We are open to a variety of backgrounds, but qualified candidates usually bring:

  • A record of building products customers love. You have the product taste and judgment to know what to build and what to leave out, and the customer empathy to find real needs before the data exists

  • Something taken from 0→1. You've built something new and gotten it to real customer pull, and you can point to the signal that proved it

  • Proven ownership of complex, cross-functional product initiatives with measurable customer and business outcomes

  • Strong product judgment and prioritization. You know what to work on, what to cut, and can drive alignment while balancing speed, quality, and learning

  • Communication and presence. You can set a vision, align an executive team, and inspire the builders who join you

  • Applied AI in your own work. You use AI and modern tooling to build and ship faster, and to go deeper across disciplines

  • Experience building and shipping AI-powered product features (bonus)

  • SaaS background, especially in products with complex operational workflows (bonus)

What Sets You Apart

The candidates who will thrive in this role go beyond strong product management:

  • You are a multidisciplinary builder. You move across product, design, engineering, and data, and you use AI to go deeper in each

  • You thrive in ambiguity. You make confident calls when there is no playbook and no data, and you follow the data the moment it exists

  • You think like an owner of the business, from the customer problem to the path to business impact, and you bring an executive team along with a clear, compelling vision

Brightwheel is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment and is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

All legitimate communications come from @mybrightwheel.com addresses, and we never ask for payment or sensitive personal data as part of our hiring process. If you suspect fraudulent contact, reach out to security@mybrightwheel.com. Thank you for helping us keep our applicant community safe.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Data Products
jobs.jd_full:
ABOUT THE TEAM

When the world's largest organizations bet on Mural, Govern & Trust is the team that earns that trust at scale. We build the experiences that help enterprises roll out Mural with confidence, keep it secure, and see the impact it has on how their people work. Data sits at the center of it all. Admins are Mural's most demanding data consumers: they need to prove ROI to their leadership, guide adoption across thousands of people, and account for every action. If data products can meet their bar, they'll work for everyone.

Mural has a modern data platform, strong data engineering and analytics teams, and a wealth of data on how teams collaborate. The next step is treating that data as a product in its own right, with a dedicated owner for what it means and how it's used.

YOUR MISSION

As a Senior Product Manager you'll define the metrics that describe how Mural creates value, and make them the shared foundation for everything built on top. The same definitions will power internal product decisions, the Insights experience Admins use in the product, and the reporting API and MCP server that customers and AI agents query.

This role starts upstream. You'll work from raw product events to decide what each metric should measure, how it's calculated, and what the data needs to look like for customers and internal teams to rely on it. Then you'll turn those metrics into experiences that help organizations understand and grow their use of Mural.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • The evolution of data products. Shape how Mural's data products move from reporting on what happened to guiding what happens next. Work across the Govern & Trust portfolio to define how insights become part of how organizations run Mural.

  • The metric layer. Define Mural's shared, cross-product metrics, like activity, collaboration, and adoption. Set the standards that let product teams define and publish their own metrics consistently. Data Engineering builds and runs the layer; you shape what goes in it and how it evolves.

  • Internal product analytics. Be a thought partner to domain PMs as they set their north-star metrics, and make product data easy for them to explore on their own. Work with Business Analytics to keep product-facing and business-facing reporting working together.

  • Customer-facing data products. Own the strategy and roadmap for Insights: in-product reporting and dashboards, exports and APIs, audit logs, and the methodology behind every number customers see.

  • AI and agent access. Package and launch Mural's customer-facing reporting MCP server: which data it exposes, which plans get it, and what guardrails apply. Define how natural-language and agent-driven analysis extends Insights.

  • Instrumentation. R&D teams own emitting events. Your job is to raise the bar on what they emit. Set per-product requirements for granularity and retention, which differ for audit logs, activity data, and product analytics. Partner with Data Engineering on event standards so metrics start from good data.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • 5+ years of product management experience, including shipping at least one analytics or reporting product used by paying business customers. You defined the metrics behind it, not just the UI.

  • A track record of making messy or conflicting data trustworthy: reconciling competing definitions, writing metric specs engineers could build from, and getting instrumentation changed upstream.

  • Experience building both platform products, where your customers are internal teams or developers, and end-user-facing data products like analytics, reporting, or insights. You understand how the two have to work together.

  • Working knowledge of modern data stacks: event pipelines, warehouses and lakehouses, dbt-style modeling, and semantic layers. You can write SQL and pull data yourself.

  • The ability to get agreement on definitions across teams you don't manage, including PMs, data engineering, analytics, finance, and go-to-market.

  • Experience with enterprise admin or governance products (IAM, security, compliance, audit)

  • Hands-on experience with semantic layer tools (dbt Semantic Layer, Cube, LookML)

  • Experience designing APIs, MCP servers, or connectors for analytics

Equal Opportunity

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Rithum™ is the world’s most trusted commerce network, accelerating how brands, suppliers, and retailers work together to deliver seamless e-commerce experiences. jobs.title: General Manager, Industrial Products & Services - US Based
jobs.jd_full:
Job Summary:

As General Manager, Industrial Products & Services (IPS), reporting directly to the EVP, Industries, you will own the strategy, growth, and profitability of Toptal’s business across Automotive, Manufacturing, Agriculture, Oil & Gas, Chemical, and Logistics clients, with full P&L and budget authority. You will identify where we can win, decide where to invest, and build the team and client relationships to deliver sustained growth. Your mandate covers winning new enterprise clients, expanding existing relationships, and increasing the value clients receive from Toptal’s capabilities.

You will bring a clear perspective on the challenges facing potential clients and where Toptal can help. Working with our Services leaders and subject matter experts, you will translate those challenges into viable sales proposals across our AI solutions, managed services, management consultancy, and talent offerings. You will choose which markets, accounts, and opportunities to pursue, allocate resources accordingly, and give your team a focused plan.

You will lead from the front: personally leading executive client conversations, shaping proposals, working through difficult commercial negotiations, and helping close critical pursuits. Your team should see the selling standard you expect in your own work. You will understand what is driving performance, where growth is constrained, and what needs to change.

You will build on established enterprise relationships to expand the problems clients trust Toptal to solve through our services, AI-based solutions, and talent-based capabilities. You will have the authority to build the team and invest in profitable growth.

This is a remote position. Applicants must be authorized to work in the US at the time of hire. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

  • Set and execute the industry strategy. Identify the markets, client problems, and offerings with the strongest growth potential. Build an IPS business plan with clear priorities, financial objectives, and investment decisions. Test your assumptions with clients and adjust the plan as evidence changes.
  • Own the P&L and budget. Be accountable for revenue, profitability, and spending. Set and manage the budget, allocate resources, and evaluate returns on investments in people and growth initiatives. Understand how pricing, delivery economics, retention, and portfolio mix affect results, and act when performance diverges from the plan.
  • Win new enterprise clients. Lead your team in pursuing priority accounts. Develop a credible reason for each client to engage with Toptal, build relationships with decision-makers, and personally advance important opportunities through discovery, solution development, negotiation, and close.
  • Expand and retain client relationships. Work with Client Partners to understand client priorities, broaden relationships across buying centers, and develop opportunities across Toptal’s portfolio. Stay close to important engagements, resolve concerns with the responsible teams, and turn successful outcomes into further business.
  • Make account planning actionable. Establish clear priorities and ownership. Expect your team to explain why an account matters, whom they need to engage, what opportunity they are pursuing, and how they will create progress. Ensure priority accounts receive sustained attention.
  • Bring the right expertise into the sale. Work with Services leaders, solution architects, and specialists to diagnose needs and develop credible proposals across services, AI-based solutions, and talent. Coordinate with supporting functions to resolve obstacles and keep opportunities moving toward a decision.
  • Maintain a credible forecast. Challenge the evidence behind opportunity values, close dates, and expected revenue. Understand the assumptions connecting the pipeline to the financial plan, identify risks early, and take specific action to address shortfalls.
  • Build and develop the team. Recruit strong commercial talent, set clear expectations, and coach people through real client situations. Review calls, account plans, and active pursuits; demonstrate stronger approaches and follow through on improvements. Address underperformance promptly and develop future leaders.
  • Accomplish work objectives through leading and supervising other Toptal team members on the Industrial Products and Services team.
  • Establish objectives and initiatives for the team, recommend the team’s structure and jobs, and organize, assign, delegate, oversee, and monitor work.
  • Coach and mentor team members, provide feedback, conduct performance reviews, and implement performance improvement plans, if needed.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Learn Toptal’s business model, capabilities, sales process, and client value proposition.
  • Meet your team and the leaders whose functions support the IPS business.
  • Begin reviewing the client portfolio, active opportunities, P&L, budget, and growth priorities.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Meet priority clients and develop an informed view of their needs, our relationships, and the opportunities ahead.
  • Assess the team’s capabilities and identify immediate coaching, performance, and hiring priorities.
  • Establish a consistent rhythm for account planning, opportunity reviews, forecasting, financial management, and coaching.
  • Present your proposed IPS business plan, including priority markets and accounts, revenue and profitability assumptions, investment choices, and the first actions you will take.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Be executing an agreed business plan with clear objectives, resource allocations, account priorities, and ownership.
  • Be personally advancing major pursuits, helping close new business, and building qualified pipelines in priority accounts, while exercising discretion and independent judgment.
  • Have specific expansion plans for key clients and be executing the talent decisions needed to strengthen the team.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Demonstrate measurable commercial progress against the plan through closed new business, expansion revenue, and margin performance.
  • Show that coaching, account planning, and opportunity reviews are improving seller performance and commercial results.
  • Manage the P&L against the budget, address material variances, and refine investment priorities using evidence from sales and delivery outcomes.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Deliver against the agreed IPS revenue, profitability, and budget objectives.
  • Have built a stronger team with clear accountability, consistent execution, and emerging leadership capability.
  • Demonstrate deeper client relationships and broader adoption of Toptal’s services, AI-based solutions, and talent-based capabilities.
  • Present the next stage of the industry business plan, including the investments required to sustain profitable growth.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree is required. Master’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred.
  • 5+ years of proven success leading professional services sales teams specifically in Industrial Products and Services, with in-depth experience in the Energy Sector, specifically Oil & Gas is required.
  • 12+ years of demonstrated experience running and managing an industry business unit with a strong understanding of business operations and management principles.
  • Deep industry relationships ranging from director-level to C-level contacts is expected.
  • A sustained record of leading enterprise SaaS or services sales teams, winning new clients, and expanding existing relationships. You can demonstrate your personal contribution to those results.
  • Industry expertise and demonstrated sales experience in at least one of Oil & Gas, Industrial Manufacturing, Automotive, or Defense & Aerospace.
  • Demonstrated accountability for commercial results and resource decisions. You can explain how your choices on pricing, hiring, investment, and account priorities affected revenue, margin, and profitability.
  • Experience closing complex enterprise opportunities, including shaping a business case, coordinating technical expertise, navigating procurement, and negotiating commercial agreements.
  • Strong industry relationships and a record of earning access to senior decision-makers through relevant insight and demonstrated value.
  • Evidence of hiring strong sellers, improving individual and team performance through specific coaching, and developing future leaders.
  • Disciplined qualification and forecasting skills. You distinguish client interest from a credible buying process, assess the evidence behind a forecast, and act when an opportunity loses momentum.
  • Sufficient fluency in technology, AI, and services delivery to discuss client priorities intelligently and recognize when deeper specialist expertise is needed.
  • Clear, persuasive written and verbal communication. You can turn a complex client problem into a compelling proposal and explain business performance without obscuring the issues.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapidly growing company and handle a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and a diverse array of contacts.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

  • Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Use all required digital collaboration tools.
  • Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

US FLSA Classification: Full-Time/Exempt

This position receives a base salary and is also eligible to earn monthly commissions based on revenue generated from engagements sold. For candidates who meet the qualifications and job requirements listed above, Individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

jobs.title: Supply Lead
jobs.jd_full:
Claru (a Reka business line) · San Francisco or remote · Full-time

Text has run out. The physical world — where skill lives — has never been recorded in a form a model can learn from. Claru is building that layer.

We sell data to frontier labs and robotics companies: zero to seven figures of ARR in under six months, with a team of five. It is a two-sided marketplace: labs arrive with a research problem and a budget, not a specification; contributors and partner businesses capture the work they already do, paid per approved unit. This job is the supply side.

We are hiring a Supply Lead and are looking for operators who are AI-native: more time with agents than with people, automation before hiring, systems that scale rather than teams that grow. That is how a team this small outruns much bigger companies. You need to be someone who can be dropped into an unfamiliar market and come back with capacity that is real.

What you'll do

  • Build a portfolio of partner businesses — whose staff capture the work they already do on shift — across the environments buyers want: event venues, retail back-of-house, construction, agriculture, hotels, warehousing. Each is won in a real conversation

  • Grow the contributor base alongside it and open new geographies, keeping supply owned and multi-channel so no single partner or geography is a dependency.

  • Own the geo rate card — what an approved unit costs by market and project type — so engagements are priced and staffed against something defensible

  • Own capacity forecasting — whether we can deliver a given volume in a given environment in a given number of weeks — which a Program Lead commits against.

  • Own contributor experience and retention: onboarding, payments landing on time, support, and why people stop.

  • Partner with the platform team on the tooling that makes supply self-serve

A typical day

There is no standard one, but a real day might run like this: you start on the partner businesses already live — chasing the ones gone quiet, calling the two that signed last month and have not filmed. Contributor payments in one market did not land, so you find where it stopped and clear it. A Program Lead needs to know whether we can cover four weeks of warehouse capture in a new country, and you give them a number you would stand behind. Then a first conversation with a food manufacturer about putting their team on shift and collecting data.

What we're looking for

  • Early-stage marketplace operating experience — required. You have got one side of a flywheel turning from a standing start, in a new territory or a new vertical — recruitment, pricing, retention and economics. Every new market here is that problem again

  • AI-native — required. You spend more time with agents than with people, you automate a process before you staff it, and your answer to more volume is a better system rather than more headcount

  • You have operated, not only advised. Former founders, high growth early stage startup hires, consulting, or business operations background is a strong plus and exactly the rigour we want

  • You close business yourself: partner businesses are won in conversation

  • Numerate — you build the model, find where the cost per unit breaks, and argue for the change

  • Credible with a company owner and with a shift supervisor alike

  • Bonus: exposure to AI labs or training data pipelines

Reka's Mission

Claru is a part of Reka (VC backed by NVIDIA). Reka's mission is to build useful multimodal artificial intelligence and use it to empower organisations and businesses. We are a globally distributed foundation model startup, headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, California. Embracing a remote-first approach, our team brings together top talent from around the world. Our founding team, along with many of our team members, has contributed to many of the breakthroughs in AI over the past decade.

Reka was founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and FAIR, and ships Reka Vision, launched in July 2026, and Reka Edge, a 7B vision-language model. Reka's leadership includes the team behind Moonvalley's Marey, the first video model trained entirely on licensed data. Claru is Reka's data business, supplying the training data behind physical AI, embodied AI and world models.

Why Reka?

  • An Elite Team: Collaborate with top-tier engineers, researchers, operators from renowned organizations like Google DeepMind and Facebook AI Research (FAIR) and successful startups, driving innovation in cutting-edge AI technology.

  • Massive Market Opportunity: Be part of a rapidly growing industry poised to transform multiple sectors globally, offering the chance to make a significant impact.

  • Mission-Driven Environment: Work alongside a collaborative, mission-focused team dedicated to advancing AI for meaningful applications.

  • Inclusive and Open Culture: Thrive in an open and inclusive work environment that values diverse perspectives and fosters creativity.

  • Generous Benefits: Enjoy 5 weeks of paid leave to recharge, comprehensive healthcare benefits including vision and dental, and additional perks that support your well-being.

Join our team

We’d love to chat to see if you’ll be an epic fit!

  • You'll grow here. Autonomy, mastery, and learning define how we work. You'll have the freedom to work on interesting problems, master new skills, and continuously develop yourself, both through your role and our personal growth fund.

  • This isn't easy, and we love that it's hard. Working at Halter will be the most rewarding and the most challenging work of your life.   • Proven ability to lead through influence across engineering, operations and commercial teams you don't manage.

  • Executive presence, including experience running steering committees and holding difficult conversations with senior customer stakeholders.

Description

🌍 Hello World!

Jesteśmy The Codest - International Tech Software Company z centrami technologicznymi w Polsce dostarczającymi globalne rozwiązania i projekty IT.

Nasze podstawowe wartości leżą w podejściu „Klienci i ludzie na pierwszym miejscu”, które stawia na pierwszym miejscu potrzeby naszych klientów i środowisko współpracy dla naszych pracowników, dzięki czemu dostarczamy naprawdę wyjątkowe produkty i usługi. Nasze doświadczenie koncentruje się na tworzeniu stron internetowych, DevOps oraz QA. Nasza misja stała się jasna po wielu latach tworzenia oprogramowania, obecnie specjalizujemy się w skalowaniu zespołów technologicznych dla klientów i partnerów.

💡Opis projektu:

Nasz klient to jedna z największych platform e-commerce w Europie, z której codziennie korzystają miliony użytkowników. Firma łączy sprzedawców – od małych biznesów po globalne marki – z klientami, oferując ogromny wybór produktów, szybkie dostawy i dopracowane doświadczenie zakupowe. Zespół rozwija skalowalne systemy o bardzo dużym natężeniu ruchu, pracuje w oparciu o dane i eksperymenty, a kultura sprzyja samodzielności, odpowiedzialności i realnemu wpływowi na rozwój produktu oraz sposób robienia zakupów w regionie.

Dołączysz do zespołu, który buduje nową platformę do planowania i uruchamiania kampanii reklamowych w wielu kanałach jednocześnie, używaną przez największe marki na rynku. System musi działać przy bardzo dużej skali ruchu, z naciskiem na wydajność, stabilność i przetwarzanie danych w czasie zbliżonym do rzeczywistego.

Product Manager jest odpowiedzialny za wartość i opłacalność (viability) tego, co buduje zespół produktowy, oraz ostatecznie ponosi odpowiedzialność za wyniki osiągane przez zespół produktowy(obejmuje również obowiązki Product Ownera).

  • Dane – uznany ekspert w zakresie danych produktowych.

  • Branża – ekspert w zakresie konkurencji, trendów rynkowych oraz trendów technologicznych.
  • Produkt – uznany ekspert w zakresie swojego produktu.

Requirements

Szukamy osoby, która ma:

  • Doświadczenie jako Product Manager (lub w podobnej roli) w branży technologicznej.
    Zainteresowanie technologią i swobodę w poruszaniu się w pojęciach takich jak React, Kotlin, Swift czy SDK.
  • Mile widziane doświadczenie w aplikacjach multiplatformowych lub no-code/low-code.
  • Silne umiejętności analityczne, decyzyjność i podejście nastawione na rozwiązywanie problemów.
  • Umiejętność patrzenia na produkt oczami użytkownika i zrozumienia potrzeb klientów.
  • Znajomość Agile oraz praktyczne doświadczenie w zarządzaniu backlogiem produktowym.
  • Doświadczenie we wdrażaniu zmian na podstawie danych, analizy oraz testów A/B.
  • Zdolność tłumaczenia potrzeb biznesowych na rozwiązania technologiczne i odwrotnie.

Na co dzień będziesz zajmować się:

  • Tworzeniem wizji produktu, roadmapy oraz planów rozwoju platformy technologicznej.
  • Współpracą z zespołami w celu zrozumienia potrzeb użytkowników i przekładania ich na nowe funkcjonalności.
  • Priorytetyzacją backlogu oraz dbaniem o to, aby prace zespołu były zgodne z celami strategicznymi.
  • Koordynacją komunikacji pomiędzy różnymi zespołami, aby wszyscy działali w jednym kierunku.

📜 Nasza oferta:

  • 23-25k PLN na B2B.
  • Płatne dni wolne w święta kalendarzowe
  • Dostęp do platformy Worksmile, gdzie co miesiąc przysługuje ci 300zł do wykorzystania na giftcardy lub różnego rodzaju usługi
  • Środowisko pracy doceniające rozwój i innowacje – ty masz pomysły, my chcemy je usłyszeć 😉

📌 Proces rekrutacyjny:

  • 30 minutowa rozmowa z naszą rekruterką, Ewą
  • 1h rozmowa techniczna z naszym CTO, Kubą
  • 1h rozmowy z klientem

Come do work that matters.

 

Senior Project Manager, Client Activation

Location: Remote (US) · Type: Full-time · Level: IC4 · Reports to: Vice President, Client & Revenue Operations

About the role

Blend’s software powers mortgage, home equity, and consumer banking for many of the largest banks, credit unions, and lenders in the US. Client Activation is the team that takes a signed customer to a live, working product.

You will own the delivery of our most complex customer engagements: Rapid home lending implementations and dedicated engineering PODs that build alongside our largest customers. It is a senior individual contributor seat. There are no direct reports. We are hiring judgment, structure and follow-through, and someone who already works AI-first.

What you will do

  • Own three to four concurrent customer engagements end to end, from kickoff through go-live, hypercare, and close.
  • Build and maintain the integrated project plan: milestones, dependencies across Blend and the customer, resourcing, and critical path.
  • Run governance: weekly status, SteerCo with customer executives, a live RAID log, and decision records.
  • Run the agile rhythm on dedicated POD engagements: sprint planning, stand-ups, retrospectives, velocity and burn-up reporting, and alignment of sprint output to SOW milestones.
  • Take over projects that are off track: rebuild the plan, set dates the team can hit, clear blockers, and drive escalations to resolution.
  • Manage scope: assess change requests, show their impact on date and effort, and route commercial changes to Deal Desk.
  • Work with Product and Engineering to get go-live blockers prioritized and resolved.
  • Keep TaskRay accurate on every project you own: health, dates, EAC, and weekly status.
  • Use AI as a core part of the job: status drafting, plan analysis and risk spotting, and help us design the next tools for Client Activation.
  • Help set the project management standard for Client Activation: templates, governance, and lessons learned that others use.

What you bring

  • Seven or more years managing customer-facing implementations of enterprise SaaS, with several projects running at once.
  • Experience delivering for banks, credit unions, mortgage lenders, or other regulated financial institutions.
  • Agile delivery experience alongside engineering teams: sprints, velocity, release planning, and backlog governance.
  • A record of recovering projects that were off track, with specifics on what you changed.
  • Executive presence: you run SteerCos, deliver bad news early with options, and hold your ground on scope.

Growth & Future

  • Pre-tax savings: healthcare & dependent care FSAs, Limited Purpose FSA, and HSA
